senses.gloss: (b. h.) [to be round and smooth,] (denom. of קֵרֵחַ) to make a bald spot.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Makkot 3:5">Macc. III, 5</cite> <he>הקוֹרִחַ קרחה וכ׳</he> he that makes a baldness upon his head.

<cite ref="Makkot 20a:12">Ib. 20ᵃ</cite> <he>יכול אפי׳ ק׳ … קריחות וכ׳</he> lest you think that even if one makes four or five spots, he is guilty only of one act; <cite ref="Kiddushin 36a:9">Kidd. 36ᵃ</cite>; a. e.

<cite ref="Mishnah Maasrot 1:3">Maasr. I, 3</cite> <he>האגסים … משיִקָּרְהוּ</he> (Y. ed. <he>משׁיַקְרִיחוּ</he>, a. <he>משיקרחו</he>) pears … are subject to tithes when their surface begins to grow smooth, v. infra.

<cite ref="Mishnah Negaim 8:5">Neg. VIII, 5</cite> <he>חזר … ונִקְרְחוּ</he> if head and chin changed and became bald; <cite ref="Tosefta Negaim 3:10">Tosef. ib. III, 10</cite> (not <he>שנ׳</he>); a. e.

<cite ref="Tosefta Ma'asrot 1:2">Tosef. Maasr. I, 2</cite> <he>משיַקְרִיחוּ</he> (not <he>משיקד׳</he>), v. supra. Y. ib. I, 48ᵈ bot. <he>משיקריחו … משיעשו קרחות … לבנות</he> ‘when they get smooth’ (Mish.
<cite ref="Mishnah Maasrot 1:3">ib. I, 3</cite>, v. supra) …, that means, when they begin to get white, smooth spots (cmp. <cite ref="S01932"><he>קְרוּחַ</he></cite>).

<cite ref="Mishnah Maasrot 1:3">Ib.</cite> <he>וכי מחמת האוכל הן מַקְרִיחִין וכ׳</he> do the fruits get white spots because of the development of the eatable matter (flesh), is it not on account of worms?; a. e.

senses.gloss: to make bare, raze. Y. Kil. IV, beg. 29ᵃ קרחת … מקריחין אותו וכ׳ ‘a bald portion of a vineyard’ (Mish.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Kilayim 4:1">ib. IV, 1</cite>) is one which is razed in the centre; <he>כרם שחרב מקריחין וכ׳</he> ‘a waste vineyard’ (ib. 2) is one which is razed on all sides.

Sot. 46ᵇ (play on קרח, II Kings II, 23) שהִקְרַחְתָּ עלינו את המקום thou hast made the place bare for us (ruined our water trade by healing the well); a. e.—Part. pass. מוּקְרָח; pl. מוּקְרָחִין. Y. Kil. I, 27ᵇ bot. ששה על ששה מוק׳ וכ׳ when one throws mixed seeds into a plot of six (cubits) by six which lies vacant within a field of grains or which is fenced in.
